info.title: governed-bi
info.summary: Health, capabilities, example questions, the pending-clarification queue and the conversation list, as JSON.
info.description:
The custom REST surface `langgraph.json` mounts at the server root, beside LangGraph Server's own routes. Spec-of-record for this surface (ADR 0007, ADR 0010).

Every route here is a read, and none of them serves a turn. A turn is served by the graph `langgraph.json` mounts, over the platform's `POST /threads/{thread_id}/runs/stream`, which is not described here. `GET /clarifications/pending` lists unanswered `ask_user` interrupts read from thread state. `GET /conversations` lists every conversation and how it ended. `GET /examples` returns few-shot questions from the corpus loaded at startup. `GET /layer` lists the schemas whose Ossie model the embedded viewer can open, and `GET /layer/{schema}` returns that model file as it is on disk.

get.description:
Process liveness. Touches neither the corpus nor the database, so it answers before the session is built. Readiness is /readyz.

It returns `{"ok": true}` and nothing else, so it reports the process's health and not that of anything the process depends on.

Readiness. Resolves the session, which under bare uvicorn is where a missing DSN, a missing corpus or a model named without its credential raises. 503 when the session cannot be built or the corpus has a fatal problem; serving with no model is a supported mode and is ready. The reason names environment variables and never carries a driver's message.
What this backend can do — the UI blocks on this response and adapts its affordances to it.

Unanswered `ask_user` interrupts, oldest first, read from LangGraph interrupt state. `meta.truncated` is set when the page window is short of the rows built or the walk stops on the 1000-thread bound. `meta.threads_scanned` is the count of distinct interrupted threads read, so an empty queue is distinguishable from a store that was not read.

Every conversation, newest first, with each turn's question and outcome and how the conversation ended, read from thread state. `ending` filters on that ending. `meta.total` counts the matching conversations before the window; `meta.truncated` is set when the window is short of them or the walk stops on the 1000-thread bound.

parameters.name: ending
parameters.description: Only conversations that ended this way.

get.description: Few-shot questions from the corpus this process loaded at startup, which are the train split. `near` ranks them with the lexical index already built for that corpus. The SQL is not returned. Without `near`, the order is by asset id.

parameters.name: near
parameters.description: Rank few-shot questions by lexical overlap with this text. Absent or blank, the list is ordered by asset id.

get.description: The schemas of the corpus this process serves that have an Ossie model file, `<schema>/<schema>.yaml`, sorted by name (ADR 0021, ADR 0022). Empty when the process serves no corpus directory.
One schema's Ossie model file, byte for byte, for the embedded viewer. Only a name `GET /layer` lists is served; any other is a 404, so no path is built from the request.

question.title: Question
question.description: Nullable. The handler passes the interrupt payload's question through, so a payload with no question key reaches the wire as null.

thread_id.title: Thread Id
thread_id.description: Nullable. The handler passes the thread's thread_id through, so a row that arrives without the field reaches the wire as null.

source.title: Source
source.description: Always `interrupt`: a live `ask_user` pause read from thread state.

interrupt_id.title: Interrupt Id
interrupt_id.description: On the wire but not in meta.columns. The interrupt's id, null when the platform carried none.

task_id.title: Task Id
task_id.description: The key of the thread's interrupts mapping. A JSON object key, so never null.

PendingClarificationRowResponse.title: PendingClarificationRowResponse
PendingClarificationRowResponse.description: One unanswered ask_user interrupt. The eight columns in PENDING_FIELDS are always present. interrupt_id and task_id are carried beside them and are not in meta.columns.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: True when this page is not everything: more rows than the window returned, or the walk stopped on the 1000-thread bound.

threads_scanned.title: Threads Scanned
threads_scanned.description: Distinct interrupted threads read to build this page. Distinguishes an empty queue from a store that was not scanned.

waiting.title: Waiting
waiting.description: A clarifying question is waiting for an answer.

ending.title: Ending
ending.description: From the last turn's outcome: `no_sql` is `answered`, `refused` and `capped` are `not_answered`, a declined clarification is `stopped`, `crashed` and a thread in `error` are `failed`. Null when no turn has finished.

question.title: Question
question.description: The most recent question, including one still waiting.

elided_turns.title: Elided Turns
elided_turns.description: Older turns the thread no longer keeps.

CapabilitiesModelsResponse.title: CapabilitiesModelsResponse
CapabilitiesModelsResponse.description: The three model surfaces this run resolved, (`api/routes.py::models_for`). All three keys are always present -- the function returns a literal three-key mapping -- so a surface with nothing resolved arrives as three nulls rather than as an absent key.

can_edit.title: Can Edit
can_edit.description: Always false: this server has no corpus write route. The corpus is edited in its own repository through review and a pinned hash.

edit_mode.title: Edit Mode
edit_mode.description: Always "none", for the same reason as can_edit.

has_live_model.title: Has Live Model
has_live_model.description: False when no agent model is configured; the graph still runs and refuses.

model.title: Model
model.description: Resolved agent model id, from `settings_resolved.chat_model` (`api/routes.py::capabilities_for`). **Not `llm_model`**, which this description named until 2026-08-22 and which `registry/settings.py` has never declared -- the string survives only inside other knobs' description text, so a client written from the old sentence went looking for a knob that does not exist. Same value as `models.agent.id`; kept as a top-level field because the header chip reads it.

can_clarify.title: Can Clarify
can_clarify.description: Clarification needs both the streaming transport and a live model.

checkpoint_durable.title: Checkpoint Durable
checkpoint_durable.description: Whether this deployment mounts a durable checkpointer. **Derived** from `langgraph.json` — `checkpointer.path` names a module and factory, and that module is on disk — so the flag goes false if either stops existing, without anyone editing a line (ADR 0009 D4). It is honest about being a *configuration reading* and not an observation: the platform injects the saver into the graph it runs and this custom app never holds that graph, so there is no live handle here to ask. Reported as the literal `False` until 2026-08-18, when `POST /chat`'s process-local `InMemorySaver` — the thing that comment described — was deleted (ADR 0014). Audit A10, `docs/open-work.md` §4.4.

hitl_survives_process_restart.title: Hitl Survives Process Restart
hitl_survives_process_restart.description:
Whether a clarification paused at `interrupt()` survives a restart of this process. Reads the same derivation as `checkpoint_durable`, and cannot be true while that is false: an `ask_user` interrupt *is* checkpoint state, and the resume reads it back out of the same store through the platform's `Command(resume=…)`, so this is one observation and not two.

**The behaviour was watched end to end on 2026-08-19**: a turn paused at `ask_user`, the process was killed and confirmed off the port, a fresh process re-mounted the prompt from checkpointed state, and answering it resumed the turn to a correct answer. So the flag is no longer derived from nothing. It is still derived from configuration rather than re-checked per process, which is what remains open. Audit A10, `docs/open-work.md` §4.4.

CapabilitiesResponse.title: CapabilitiesResponse
CapabilitiesResponse.description: What this server can actually do. The UI blocks on it, so every key is always present.

id.title: Id
id.description: The model id, read out of `settings_resolved` rather than off the live client, so it is the identity a run is actually recorded under. `agent.id` is the `chat_model` knob and `utility.id` is `llm_utility_model`. Null when nothing resolved one -- an offline profile with no model wired.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Which gateway served the id (`llm_provider` / `llm_utility_provider`). Carried beside the id and never folded into it: the same id behind two gateways is two treatments. Both knobs default to `openai`, so this is null only when `settings_resolved` carries no entry at all.

effort.title: Effort
effort.description: Reasoning effort in the engine's vocabulary. `agent.effort` is the `llm_reasoning_effort` knob; `utility.effort` is **observed off the live client** by `model/provider.py::reasoning_effort_of`, because the register declares no utility-effort knob. Null means either no live utility client or a client that sends no reasoning configuration -- a real state, not a failure to look.

ModelSurfaceResponse.title: ModelSurfaceResponse
ModelSurfaceResponse.description: One chat surface's resolved identity (`api/routes.py::models_for`). Every field is present and every field is nullable.

id.title: Id
id.description: The `embedding_model` knob, **provider-qualified** (`bedrock:amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`) and reported verbatim. Do not split it on `:` -- the qualifier is part of the vector cache-key identity (`retrieve.semantic.cache_key` is `model|dimensions|text`) and the id itself can contain a colon, so parsing it corrupts the one field that keeps two gateways' vectors apart.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: The `embedding_provider` knob, carried beside the qualified id rather than parsed out of it.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.description: The `embedding_dimensions` knob -- the served width, probed off the embedder (`model/embedder.py` records `int(embedder.dimensions)`) rather than declared. Null when no embedder resolved.

EmbeddingSurfaceResponse.title: EmbeddingSurfaceResponse
EmbeddingSurfaceResponse.description: The embedding surface (`api/routes.py::models_for`). Same three-key shape as a chat surface, with `dimensions` where a chat surface carries `effort`.

dialect.title: Dialect
dialect.description: Always present: every connector declares one, and the handler falls back to `postgres` for a partial session.

host.title: Host
host.description: **Absent, not null**, when the connector's endpoint does not carry one -- SQLite is a file, and Postgres omits any DSN field it could not parse. `datasource/postgres.py::endpoint` stringifies every value it emits.

port.title: Port
port.description: A **string**, not a number: `datasource/postgres.py::endpoint` emits `str(value)` for host, port and database alike. Absent for SQLite and for an unparseable DSN.

database.title: Database
database.description: The database name, or for SQLite the file name rather than the absolute path. Absent when the endpoint does not carry one.

ConnectionResponse.title: ConnectionResponse
ConnectionResponse.description: Which warehouse this engine is pointed at (`api/routes.py::connection_for`), **credential-free by construction**: the redaction lives in the connector that owns the DSN (`datasource/postgres.py::endpoint`), which never parses `user` or `password` out at all, so there is no field here for a caller to leak. Only `dialect` is guaranteed -- the other three are whatever `connector.endpoint` returned, and an unparseable DSN returns an empty mapping.

question.title: Question
question.description: The few-shot question (`FewShotAsset.summary`). The body, which repeats the SQL, is not returned.

db_id.title: Db Id
db_id.description: The database the few-shot belongs to (`FewShotAsset.schema`).
